clue.text: Seeking to gain our trust? Not our trust!

definitions.text: Seeking to gain our trust? Not our trust!

parts.note: surface reading: a con artist trying to win our confidence
setter's reading: our trust, a charitable body, is not after profit at all

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to win our confidence, and an indignant voice denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'trust' is confidence; the second is a charitable trust, which by law does not trade for gain.
explanation.definitionFit: A charity or trust exists for a cause rather than for earnings, so it is described as non-profit-making.

clue.text: Making sense of the accounts department?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: being logical, as in 'it doesn't add up'

definitions.note: names who does it, not the activity
definitions.meaning: second meaning: totting figures, what that department spends its day doing

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the finance office has a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for being coherent and also literally describes summing columns of figures.

clue.text: Sloth, for some of you, a nuclear upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the run of letters over so it reads bottom to top
only some of the following words' letters are wanted, a run straddling their boundaries

parts.note: the run sits across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A sloth is apparently upset by something nuclear.
explanation.walkthrough: The unau is the two-toed sloth of South America, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: The unau is a species of tree-dwelling South American mammal, the two-toed sloth.

clue.text: Polonius was behind it, e'en perhaps in its material

parts.note: in Hamlet, Polonius hides behind a wall tapestry and is stabbed through it

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word e'en is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: the poetic contraction of even, letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A literary aside about the tapestry Polonius hid behind and what it was made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrasene is an embroidery thread or fabric of wool and silk, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Bird echoing a little timid cry

indicators.note: an echo comes back the way it went, so the built word is read in the opposite direction
only a little of the next word is kept, its opening couple of letters

parts.note: the opening two letters of the word
to cry is to weep

explanation.surface: A bird gives out a small, nervous call.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is named after its call, so the surface is also a fair description of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit is another name for the lapwing, a plover named for its plaintive call.

clue.text: Here other crossword compilers bundle me with Achilles's old lady

definitions.note: a place where they work, not the compilers themselves

indicators.note: to bundle one thing with another is to wrap it up inside

parts.note: the sea nymph Thetis was the mother of Achilles; old lady is slang for mother
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rival paper's setters lump the speaker in with a figure from Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunthorne set for the Guardian, so 'here' is a rival paper, The Times, famous for its own cryptic crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: The London daily newspaper employs a separate team of setters for its renowned cryptic puzzle.

clue.text: Stables needing a day to clean and a month to labour

definitions.text: Stables needing a day to clean

parts.note: the abbreviation for August
an old verb meaning to bring forth young, as in yean

explanation.surface: Filthy stables that take a day to clean and a month of hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like toil but means giving birth; EAN is an archaic word for lambing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules cleaned King Augeas's filthy stables in a single day as one of his twelve labours.

clue.text: Barman hurrying to take your suit to the cleaners. Ach! A bum steer!

definitions.text: Barman hurrying to take your suit to the cleaners

parts.words: Barman hurrying to take your suit to the cleaners.
parts.note: surface reading: a pub worker rushing off with your clothes for dry cleaning
setter's reading: a member of the Bar rushing after accident victims to bring a lawsuit and fleece the defendant

explanation.surface: A bartender dashes off with your suit for cleaning, and a Scots voice calls it bad advice.
explanation.walkthrough: A barman here is a barrister, a suit is a lawsuit, and taking someone to the cleaners is stripping them of money. A bum steer is misleading guidance, the exclamation warns the surface is false.
explanation.definitionFit: The derogatory term describes a lawyer who chases injury victims to solicit compensation claims.

clue.text: Guillotined, you badly need a way into a Belgian hanging

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of the other
something done badly is muddled, so the next word's letters are disordered
guillotining removes the head, so the following word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before beheading
taken as written before mixing
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A grim picture of an execution in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guillotined' and 'hanging' suggest executions, but the hanging is a tapestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Oudenarde, a Flemish town, was famous for woven tapestries, so its name is used for one such wall hanging.

clue.text: Cart a lot of straw

parts.note: to cart something is to haul it
M, a thousand in Roman numerals, stands for a large number

explanation.surface: Someone carts off a large load of straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Haulm is the stalks or stems of crops such as beans or potatoes, used like straw for thatch or litter.

clue.text: Toffee-nosed and, you'll aver, a slip of a cow for one

definitions.text: slip of a cow for one
definitions.note: an example of the plant genus

parts.note: toffee-nosed, British slang for snooty, is close to prim and proper

indicators.note: to aver is to declare out loud, so the word you'll counts for its sound

parts.note: the contraction is said like the letters UL in the middle of the plant's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snooty person declares something about a young cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A slip of a cow' is really cowslip, a member of the primrose genus.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip belongs to the genus Primula, so it is one example of a primula.

clue.text: He painted with a dry water

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written
TT, teetotal, describes someone who stays off drink
the French word for water

explanation.surface: An artist working with a dry brush in watercolour.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine Watteau was the French Rococo artist known for his scenes of fetes galantes.

clue.text: Only Lenin, Gorbachev and, initially, this female comrade?

indicators.note: initially means taking only the first letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the opening letter
the opening letter
the opening letter
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A wry question about which Soviet figures belong in the same club as one woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Olga is a typically Russian girl's name, fitting for a woman in a Soviet setting.

clue.text: Old English claimant yielding to old Welsh fervour?

indicators.note: yielding means producing, as these letters produce a new word once rearranged

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for Old English
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claimant from England backs down before a passionate Welsh opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yielding' looks like giving way, but here it means producing. The question mark flags old Welsh as only one example of the Celtic.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtomania is an enthusiasm for all things Celtic, such as ancient Welsh language and culture.

clue.text: Bunthorne's out of date? No way!

parts.note: the setter is speaking of himself: I'm
passé is French for past it or old-fashioned

explanation.surface: The setter asks if he is past it and indignantly denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter naming himself stands for 'I am', the usual crossword convention for 'setter'.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock where there is no way forward, a blocked route.

clue.text: The French when in Kent, having right to be profligate

indicators.note: one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
quand is the French word for when
the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: French visitors in Kent are entitled to spend freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' looks like LE or LA, but it signals translating the next word into French.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander is to spend money wastefully and recklessly, which is what profligate people do.

clue.text: Many a game hedgehog lodges thus?

definitions.note: describes how certain lodges are, rather than naming them

parts.note: M, a thousand in Roman numerals, stands for many
taken as written
Sonic the Hedgehog is the Sega video-game character

explanation.surface: A question whether lots of plucky hedgehogs shelter in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodges' looks like a verb about where hedgehogs sleep; it is a noun, the meeting places of Freemasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons meet in branches called lodges, so such lodges are described by this adjective.

clue.text: Brood mare is, to a stallion, correct in this

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, which this refers back to

parts.note: a mare is a stallion's partner
to correct a text is to edit it

explanation.surface: A horse-breeding note about a brood mare and her stallion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brood mare' reads as one phrase, but 'Brood' is the verb on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To brood is to ponder something at length, which is close to deep contemplation.

clue.text: Not behind society, when all have equal rights

parts.note: taken as written
a behind is the rump
the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A political slogan about a society with no one left behind and equal rights.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, no-trumps means no suit outranks the others, so every suit is equal.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract played in bridge without a trump suit gives all four suits equal standing.

clue.text: Play with dominoes made out of square pieces

indicators.note: broken into pieces, the letters are scattered and put back together differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A game played with dominoes cut from square tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: A domino is also a cloak with a half-mask worn at masked balls, not just a game tile.
explanation.definitionFit: A masked ball is a festive pretence where guests wear disguises such as the domino mask.

clue.text: The pong of sulphur and fish

parts.note: the chemical symbol for sulphur
the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: The rotten-egg reek of sulphur mixed with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Pong is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong unpleasant odour, which is exactly what slang calls a pong.

clue.text: Return to the keyboard for tyre-changing training

indicators.note: changing the word tyre means altering the order of its letters

parts.note: taken as written
PE is physical education, school exercise training

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to typing after a tyre-changing course.
explanation.definitionFit: To retype is to key a text in again, going back to the typewriter or computer for another go.

clue.text: One's into prescription-free sales, according to the auditor

definitions.note: means relating to the ear, the hearer's organ

indicators.note: one piece is put into the middle of the other

parts.note: OTC, over the counter, describes medicines sold without a prescription
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A pharmacy audit reports on someone moving into over-the-counter sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant, but it is a listener, so the definition is about hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective for the ear, the part a listener hears with.

clue.text: Salar held in suspense here?

parts.note: surface reading: someone named Salar kept waiting anxiously
setter's reading: Salmo salar, the Atlantic salmon, is kept alive in a net hanging in the water by an angler

explanation.surface: Someone waits nervously for news in some place.
explanation.walkthrough: Salar is the Latin species name of the salmon, and 'in suspense' means literally suspended in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's long mesh bag, suspended in the river, keeps caught fish alive until release.

clue.text: Rump chops in tea: it's on the menu in Tokyo

definitions.text: it's on the menu in Tokyo

indicators.note: the mixed letters go in the middle of the other word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: chopping something up breaks it apart, so the word's letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written before mixing

explanation.surface: Steak chops served with tea in a Japanese restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is battered, deep-fried seafood or vegetables, a classic Japanese restaurant dish.

clue.text: Undertaker's assistant married Amerindian

parts.note: the abbreviation for married
the Ute are a Native American people of Utah and Colorado

explanation.surface: A funeral director's helper married a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: A mute was a hired mourner who walked silently with a Victorian funeral procession for the undertaker.

clue.text: Ulster revolutionary finding job satisfaction in this

definitions.note: a place, rather than a phrase meaning contentment

parts.note: Ulster is used for Northern Ireland, NI
Che Guevara is the crossword's favourite revolutionary

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish rebel turns out to enjoy his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding your niche means landing in a role that suits you, where work becomes fulfilling.

clue.text: Food apposite to cooking: but no seconds offered!

indicators.note: cooking treats the ingredients so they come out in a new form
seconds is read as the letter S, the abbreviation for a second, which is left out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dish that suits being cooked, but nobody gets a second helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like second helpings; it is the S that comes out before the letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie topped or filled with potatoes is a hearty dish, a plain example of food.
